The unit has two files. src/products/application/index.ts is empty. src/products/application/sagas/product.saga.ts holds one class, ProductSaga, which handles one concern: orchestrating product domain events through NestJS CQRS sagas. Its three handlers (productCreated, productPriceChanged, productStatusChanged) all use the same ofType/delay/map pattern on domain events from the product aggregate. They don't split into unrelated concerns. They don't step around the module's own abstractions, because the module has no other abstractions to step around.

The handlers repeat a 1000ms delay and the `return null as any` placeholder. Those are repeated stub boilerplate, not a business rule or invariant written in two places. The only check that looks like a rule is `productStatus === 'INACTIVE'`, and it appears once. Returning `null as any` where `Observable<ICommand>` is expected is a weak spot for type safety and correctness, but it doesn't break module cohesion.

The empty application-level index.ts doesn't re-export sagas/index.ts. That inconsistency is minor and doesn't create a second concern. Overall the unit passes.
